summary: Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and as Professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).

Julius Euting specialized in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen under Ernst Heinrich Meier and Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Director of the Bibliothèque nationale et universitaire (1871, 1900–1909) and professor at Strasbourg (1880).

Julius Grill was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and earned a Lic. theol. at Jena. He served as professor of Old Testament exegesis at Tübingen (1888–1913).

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Leipzig, completing his PhD under Martin Haug. He served as Tagore Professor at Calcutta (1882–1883) and long-term professor at the University of Würzburg (1877–1920).

Julius Lipner is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Jadavpur, Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. He taught at the University of Birmingham before serving as Professor of Hinduism at the University of Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Sinological studies. After studying at Tübingen and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, he held posts at Tübingen, the Société Asiatique, and the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Müller was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Breslau, Berlin, and Göttingen. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1834), University of Marburg (~1834–1839), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).

Julius Pokorny worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much. He held posts at Vienna (~1913–1920), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1935), University of Bern (~1944–1948), and University of Zurich (~1944–1970).
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Bonn (~1857–1858), the University of Göttingen (~1858–1860), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1860–1862).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctoral degree in literature at the University of Tokyo (~2000–2005). He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University (~2011–2017).

Jun Takashima is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He held posts at Aichi Prefectural University and served as Professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2020).

Jun Yang is a scholar in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Yang has served as a Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

Jundo Nagashima is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, also studying under Seitatsu Matsunami and Alexis Sanderson. He has held research and lecturer posts at Taisho University.

June McDaniel is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served on the faculty at the College of Charleston, attested between 2000 and 2015.

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dongguk University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2012) under Harunaga Isaacson. She also served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Ha earned a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe, attested in 2016.

Junjirō Takakusu was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served as professor and president at the University of Tokyo.
Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at Toyo University (~1887–1891). He later served as a professor at Toyo University and Komazawa University.

Junkichi Imanishi is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He served as associate professor at Hokkaido University, Chancellor of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and Director of the IIBS.

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at the Australian National University (1980) and a doctorate at the University of Göttingen (1990). Matsumura is attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
